skills.name: joinLines
skills.card:
joinLines — Join the lines of a text into one line, separated by a delimiter you choose.
  needs: text: string
  optional: delimiter: string, skipBlank: boolean, trim: boolean
  e.g. "join these lines with commas" → {"text":"apple\nbanana\ncherry"}
examples: turn this list into a comma separated line
join the lines with a pipe
join lines and skip the empty ones
join into a sentence with and

skills.name: keywordsTfidf
skills.card:
keywordsTfidf — Pull the most distinctive words out of a document.
  needs: text: string
  optional: limit: integer, corpus: array
  e.g. "pull the keywords out of this" → {"text":"The pigeon carried the message. Pigeons have carried messages for centuries. The message arrived safely.","limit":4}

text.label: text
text.prompt: Which text should I pull keywords from?

corpus.label: other documents
corpus.description: other documents to score against - the text is split into its own sections if none are given

examples: pull the keywords out of this
what are the main topics here

skills.name: lexiconSentiment
examples: score the sentiment of this feedback
is this message positive or negative
analyse the tone of this comment
would you say this comes across as cheerful or gloomy
is the tone of this positive or negative

skills.name: maskSensitive
skills.card:
maskSensitive — Hide private details in text — emails, phone numbers, cards — behind placeholders.
  needs: text: string
  optional: style: string, kinds: array
  e.g. "redact the personal data in this" → {"text":"Contact ana@example.com or call 020 7946 0958."}

kinds.label: kinds to mask
kinds.description: limit the masking to these kinds

examples: redact the personal data in this
mask this card number with stars
scrub the email and phone number out of this
blank out the personal information here

skills.name: normalizeWhitespace
skills.card:
normalizeWhitespace — Tidy the spacing in a text — collapse runs of spaces, trim the ends, and unify line endings.
  needs: text: string
  optional: collapseBlankLines: boolean
  e.g. "tidy up the spacing in this" → {"text":"too    many     spaces"}

collapseBlankLines.label: collapse blank lines
collapseBlankLines.description: reduce runs of blank lines to one

examples: tidy up the spacing in this
clean up text pasted from a pdf

skills.name: numberLines
skills.card:
numberLines — Put a line number in front of each line of a text.
  needs: text: string
  optional: start: integer, separator: string, skipBlank: boolean
  e.g. "number these lines" → {"text":"alpha\nbeta\ngamma"}
examples: number a ten line list to check the padding

skills.name: padText
skills.card:
padText — Pad text out to a fixed width, aligned left, right or centre.
  needs: text: string, width: integer
  optional: align: string, fill: string
  e.g. "pad "abc" to 8 characters" → {"text":"abc","width":8}
examples: pad with dots to make a table of contents line
pad text that is already too long

skills.name: readingLevel
examples: how hard is this to read
flesch score for a plain paragraph
grade level of a short instruction

skills.name: readingTime

skills.name: removeDuplicateLines
skills.card:
removeDuplicateLines — Remove repeated lines from a text, keeping the first time each one appeared.
  needs: text: string
  optional: ignoreCase: boolean, ignoreSpacing: boolean
  e.g. "remove the duplicate lines" → {"text":"apple\nbanana\napple\ncherry"}

ignoreSpacing.label: ignore spacing
ignoreSpacing.description: treat lines differing only in spacing as the same

examples: dedupe this list keeping the order
strip repeated lines from text that has none

skills.name: removeEmoji
skills.card:
removeEmoji — Strip emoji out of text.
  needs: text: string
  optional: replaceWith: string
  e.g. "remove the emoji from this" → {"text":"Great work 👍 thanks 🎉"}

text.label: text
text.prompt: Which text should I strip emoji from?

examples: take the emoji out of this message
remove emoji and keep the words

skills.name: removeStopWords
skills.card:
removeStopWords — Strip the common filler words from a text, leaving only the content words.
  needs: text: string
  optional: extra: array
  e.g. "strip the filler words from this" → {"text":"the cat sat on the mat"}

extra.label: extra words to remove
extra.description: more words to treat as filler

examples: strip the filler words from this
remove stop words from a search query
strip filler and my own extra words
remove stop words when there are none
strip a sentence that is all filler

skills.name: replaceText
skills.card:
replaceText — Find and replace text, either literally or with a regular expression.
  needs: text: string, find: string, replace: string
  optional: regex: boolean, caseSensitive: boolean
  e.g. "replace "colour" with "color" in my text" → {"text":"The colour of the colour chart.","find":"colour","replace":"color"}

replace.label: replace with
replace.prompt: What should I replace it with?

examples: swap all the commas for semicolons
collapse repeated spaces using a regex
replace something that is not there

skills.name: reverseText
skills.card:
reverseText — Reverse a text — by character, by word, or by line.
  needs: text: string
  optional: by: string
  e.g. "reverse the word stressed" → {"text":"stressed"}
examples: reverse the word order of the quick brown fox

skills.name: similarityJaccard
skills.card:
similarityJaccard — Measure how much two texts overlap by the words they share.
  needs: a: string, b: string
  optional: caseSensitive: boolean
  e.g. "how similar are these two sentences" → {"a":"the quick brown fox","b":"the quick red fox"}
examples: how similar are these two sentences

skills.name: similarityLevenshtein
skills.card:
similarityLevenshtein — Measure how many single-character edits turn one string into another, and how similar that makes them.
  needs: a: string, b: string
  optional: caseSensitive: boolean
  e.g. "how different are kitten and sitting" → {"a":"kitten","b":"sitting"}
examples: how different are kitten and sitting
edit distance between colour and color
how similar are these two names

skills.name: slugify
skills.card:
slugify — Turn a title into a URL-safe slug — lowercase, hyphens, no accents or punctuation.
  needs: text: string
  optional: separator: string, maxLength: integer
  e.g. "make a slug from "Hello, World! A Beginner's Guide"" → {"text":"Hello, World! A Beginner's Guide"}

text.label: text
text.prompt: What should I turn into a slug?

examples: make a slug from "Hello, World! A Beginner's Guide"
url slug for "Café Münster — Opening Times"
slugify with underscores: My Blog Post
short slug, max 12 chars, from "The Complete Guide To Everything"

skills.name: sortLines
skills.card:
sortLines — Put the lines of a text in order — alphabetically, numerically, or by length.
  needs: text: string
  optional: by: string, direction: string, caseSensitive: boolean
  e.g. "sort these lines alphabetically" → {"text":"cherry\napple\nbanana"}
examples: sort this list z to a

skills.name: splitLines
skills.card:
splitLines — Split one line into separate lines wherever a delimiter appears.
  needs: text: string
  optional: delimiter: string, trim: boolean, skipBlank: boolean
  e.g. "split this comma separated list onto lines" → {"text":"apple, banana, cherry"}
examples: split this comma separated list onto lines
split and drop the empty pieces

skills.name: stemWords
examples: stem short words that should not change

skills.name: stripHtml
skills.card:
stripHtml — Strip the tags out of HTML markup and leave the readable words. needs: html: string optional: keepLineBreaks: boolean e.g. "strip the tags from

Hello world

" → {"html":"

Hello world

"}
examples: get the text out of this html
remove tags and decode the entities
strip a script tag and its contents
strip html with a line break
drop the tags and give me the plain words from this html
remove the html and leave the words

skills.name: stripMarkdown
skills.card:
stripMarkdown — Turn markdown into plain text, dropping the formatting marks.
  needs: markdown: string
  optional: keepLinkText: boolean
  e.g. "strip the markdown from **bold** and *italic*" → {"markdown":"**bold** and *italic*"}
examples: strip inline code and a code fence

skills.name: syllableCount
examples: syllables in the quick brown fox
count the beats when you say banana out loud

skills.name: toAscii
skills.card:
toAscii — Strip accents and convert a text to plain ASCII.
  needs: text: string
  optional: dropUnknown: boolean
  e.g. "convert café to ascii" → {"text":"café"}

dropUnknown.label: drop unconvertible
dropUnknown.description: remove characters with no ASCII equivalent

examples: strip the accents from Münster Straße
convert smart quotes to plain ones
convert text that is already ascii

skills.name: tokenizeSentences
tokenizeWords
skills.card:
tokenizeWords — Break a sentence at its spaces into separate words.
  needs: text: string
  optional: lowercase: boolean, unique: boolean
  e.g. "split this into words" → {"text":"The quick brown fox"}

skills.name: trimLines
skills.card:
trimLines — Remove the leading and trailing spaces from every line of a text, leaving the lines themselves in place.
  needs: text: string
  optional: dropBlank: boolean
  e.g. "trim the spaces off each line" → {"text":"  one  \n  two\nthree   "}

dropBlank.label: drop blank lines
dropBlank.description: also remove lines that end up empty

examples: trim the spaces off each line
trim lines and drop the empty ones
trim lines that are already clean

skills.name: truncateText
skills.card:
truncateText — Cut text off at a maximum length and end it with an ellipsis.
  needs: text: string, limit: integer
  optional: unit: string, ellipsis: string, breakWords: boolean
  e.g. "shorten this to 20 characters" → {"text":"The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog","limit":20}

breakWords.label: cut mid-word
breakWords.description: allow cutting in the middle of a word

examples: truncate a string already short enough
shorten to 10 chars with a custom ellipsis
truncate mid-word if it has to

skills.name: wordFrequency
skills.card:
wordFrequency — Which words repeat most in a text — each distinct word ranked by how often it recurs.
  needs: text: string
  optional: limit: integer, removeStopWords: boolean
  e.g. "what words come up most in this text" → {"text":"the cat sat on the mat the cat purred","limit":2}
examples: what words come up most in this text
most common words including the small ones
word counts for a repeated phrase
top word in a sentence about testing
frequency when every word is a stop word

skills.name: wrapText
skills.card:
wrapText — Hard-wrap text to a maximum line width, breaking lines at a set number of characters.
  needs: text: string
  optional: width: integer, indent: string
  e.g. "wrap this at 20 characters" → {"text":"The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog","width":20}
examples: wrap a paragraph keeping the blank line
reflow this so no line passes 16 characters
